#!/bin/bash

# System Limits Configuration Script
# This script configures various system limits and resource controls

# Memory limits
MAX_MEMORY_MB=8192        # Maximum memory in MB
MIN_MEMORY_MB=512         # Minimum memory in MB
SWAP_SIZE_MB=2048         # Swap space size in MB

# CPU limits
MAX_CPU_CORES=16          # Maximum CPU cores
CPU_FREQUENCY_MHZ=3600    # CPU frequency in MHz
MAX_LOAD_AVERAGE=8.0      # Maximum load average

# File system limits
MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB=1024     # Maximum file size in MB
MAX_OPEN_FILES=65536      # Maximum open files
MAX_INODES=1000000        # Maximum inodes

# Network limits
MAX_CONNECTIONS=10000     # Maximum network connections
MAX_BANDWIDTH_MBPS=1000   # Maximum bandwidth in Mbps
CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_SEC=30 # Connection timeout in seconds

# Process limits
MAX_PROCESSES=4096        # Maximum number of processes
MAX_THREADS=8192          # Maximum number of threads
PROCESS_PRIORITY=0        # Default process priority (nice value)

# Security limits
MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=5      # Maximum login attempts
SESSION_TIMEOUT_MIN=30    # Session timeout in minutes
MAX_SUDO_TIMEOUT_MIN=15   # Maximum sudo timeout in minutes

# Logging limits
MAX_LOG_SIZE_MB=512       # Maximum log file size in MB
MAX_LOG_FILES=10          # Maximum number of log files
LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=30     # Log retention period in days

apply_limits() {
    echo "Applying system limits..."
    ulimit -n $MAX_OPEN_FILES
    ulimit -u $MAX_PROCESSES
    echo "System limits applied successfully"
}

check_limits() {
    echo "Current system limits:"
    ulimit -a
}

# Main execution
if [ "$1" == "apply" ]; then
    apply_limits
elif [ "$1" == "check" ]; then
    check_limits
else
    echo "Usage: $0 [apply|check]"
fi
